chunks: My father narrated, may God be pleased with him, saying: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated to us, from his father, from Hammad, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Prostration is performed on seven bones: the forehead, the two palms, the two knees, and the two big toes, and you press your nose to the ground. As for the obligatory part, these are the seven, and as for the pressing of the nose, it is Sunnah.

key_terms.تُرْغَمُ بِنَافِكَ: pressing the nose to the ground

ai.seo_question: What are the seven bones required for prostration in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) clarifies the jurisprudential distinction between the seven obligatory contact points (fard) and the recommended pressing of the nose (taraghham) during prostration, a ruling derived from the verse 'Fall prostrate and draw near' (96:19). This hadith from al-Khisal underscores the Shia emphasis on both the physical completeness of the prayer posture and the spiritual humility it represents, with the nose serving as a symbol of closeness to the Divine.
